newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen opening under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen opening under pressure.

* Toronto stocks were expected to open under pressure as weak bonds and the Canadian dollar weighed on the market * Analysts said golds may help offset negatives in the choppy session.
Toronto stocks were expected to open under pressure on Wednesday as weak North American bonds and the Canadian dollar weigh on the market.
Analysts said the market will likely be unsettled today after the roller-coaster ride down on Monday and up on Tuesday, but golds may help offset losses as the price of bullion rose.
"I think the TSE is going to open under modest pressure, and I think we are going to get a choppy day," said MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie.
Toronto's key 300 Composite Index traded on both sides of unchanged yesterday, ending up 53.25 points at 6490.96.
New York's Dow Jones Industrial Average staged a 153-point rebound from Monday's 192-point sell-off.

Beattie said rising spot gold prices should help the battered gold sector, which led losing sub-indexes yesterday, but interest-sensitives will likely sink with the bond market. "Banks will probably suffer a bit because of the weakness in the Canadian dollar and our yields are backing up -- bonds are down and bills are down so yields are backing up -- so that's negative for interest-sensitive stocks," Beattie said.
The banking sector caught the spotlight on Tuesday as takeover news hit the market.
Bank of Nova Scotia, the nation's fourth largest, rose 2.25 to a new 52-week high of 60.05 after news that it offered to acquire National Trustco Inc in a deal valued at C$1.25 billion.

Also centre stage was London Insurance Group, after it said it was in talks with the country's largest bank, Royal Bank of Canada. London Insurance added 2.80 to 26.30 while Royal Bank edged up 1.15 to a 52-week record of 63.15.
In economic news, Canada's composite leading indicator rose 0.7 percent in May to 193.3 (base 1981) after a 0.8 percent rise in April, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday.
A Reuter survey of economists had forecast the index to rise 0.8 percent.

StatsCan also said today the preliminary estimate of average weekly earnings for Canadian workers in all industries except agriculture and fishing rose 4.0 percent in April from a year earlier to a seasonally adjusted C$599.88.
From the month before, earnings rose 0.6 percent.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast that average weekly earnings would rise by 3.0 percent, year on year, after a 2.7 percent rise in March.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---

* The battle between Crystallex International Corp and Placer Dome Inc over the lucrative Las Cristinas gold property in Venezuela may be resolved soon as each side looks to the Venezuelan Supreme Court to rule in its favor. Crystallex stock began trading on the American Stock Exchange Tuesday.
